# AGENTS-STARTUP.md — AI Session Protocol for YITC v2

This file is a **SOURCE** the primary AI agent's startup seed is assembled from — read at every session start AND after every `/compact` — a Worker via its assembled VIEW (`graph/worker-seed.md` **and every continuation part it chains to**); the Controller reads the SOURCE parts directly in the read-order (each single-read-safe — SPEC-0007 §5c). It defines what the AI does, in what order, with what discipline.

**After a context compaction:** unless a `RESTORATION BRIEF` is already in your context (the in-repository post-compaction entry prints it), FIRST run `bin/yitc-v2 session start --print-only` — the brief, it stamps nothing — then follow §After `/compact`.

## At session start (BEFORE any tool call)

**Handbook SOURCE manifest** — the read-order the interactive Controller reads DIRECTLY, part by part, and the generation
order a dispatched Worker's assembled VIEW is built from (a Worker reads that view, NOT these files one-by-one — §Per-audience read-order below):

<!--GEN:read-order:numbered GENERATED from HANDBOOK_READ_ORDER in bin/yitc-v2 — DO NOT EDIT; regen via `bin/yitc-v2 graph build` (SPEC-0007 §5b)-->
1. **CHARTER.md** — the 8 principles + non-goals. Anti-complexity (principle #1) governs every subsequent decision.
2. **AGENTS-STARTUP.md** — this protocol file — what the AI does, in what order, with what discipline (part 1 of 3).
3. **AGENTS-SESSIONS.md** — session types + write-flow + scope boundary — part 2 of the AGENTS protocol (a separate startup-served file, read it after AGENTS-STARTUP.md).
4. **AGENTS-PROTOCOL.md** — worker protocol, gates, filing, planning & references — part 3 of the AGENTS protocol (a separate startup-served file, read it after AGENTS-SESSIONS.md).
5. **LIFECYCLE.md** — the 9-stage task lifecycle. You'll work through one of these stages per session turn.
6. **QUEUE.md** — where tasks live (active / done / parking-lot). Source of truth for «what to do next».
7. **GRAPH.md** — how specs link to code. Use before designing anything new (Principle 1 filter (1) «existing analog?»).

The files in this read-order — the generated `HANDBOOK_READ_ORDER` set — ARE the handbook (<vendor-adapter>.md is a vendor adapter pointing here, NOT counted in the canonical handbook cap per CHARTER §Principle 2). The AGENTS protocol is SPLIT across **AGENTS-STARTUP.md + AGENTS-SESSIONS.md + AGENTS-PROTOCOL.md** for single-Read safety (SPEC-0120); a Worker receives all parts inside its assembled view, the Controller reads them directly as source parts of the read-order (§Per-audience read-order below). Held within the CHARTER §Principle 2 size budget, which counts the FULL generated set incl every split part (the authoritative home — the cap number is not restated here, so it cannot diverge). Read the WHOLE of your audience's seed.

**Per-audience read-order (SPEC-0007 §5c + SPEC-0127).** The read-order above IS the interactive Controller's runtime read — it reads the SOURCE parts DIRECTLY, in that order (its audience union = ALL sections = these files, each single-read-safe; no assembled monolith — SPEC-0007 §5c; the generated `graph/controller-supplement.md` stays a derived reference view, not a runtime read). A **dispatched Worker** (`--type build`) reads the SMALLER slice: its whole startup handbook is the generated `core`+`worker` seed, also **IN PLACE OF** the full files above. **That seed is a CHAIN of size-bounded parts, not one file :** read **`graph/worker-seed.md`** and then **every continuation part it names** (`graph/worker-seed-2.md` …) — part 1 lists the whole chain, and each part points at its next hop. The chain exists because a GENERATED startup read surface is held to the same one-bounded-read ceiling as a source doc (SPEC-0007 §5c / SPEC-0120 §3). **One part is NOT the seed** — stopping early silently starves you of rules. This routing is delivered on BOTH load surfaces: the manual read-order (here — this note is itself `core`, so a Worker sees it inside part 1 of its seed) AND the vendor auto-inject (the engine `<vendor-adapter>.md` names the same chain, so a Worker's `worktree new`+`cd` re-floors exactly `core`+`worker`).

**Kernel-prefixed retrieval under `-C` (SPEC-0092).** Every handbook retrieved-tier pointer
(`graph query SPEC-XXXX`) names a KERNEL spec by its bare id. In a `-C <consumer>` session that owns its
OWN spec at the SAME id, a bare `graph query SPEC-XXXX` resolves the CONSUMER's spec (consumer-own wins) — so to fetch the kernel contract the pointer names, re-issue it with **`--kernel`**:
`bin/yitc-v2 graph query --kernel SPEC-XXXX` (forces the engine/kernel spec + body). In the engine's own session `--kernel` is a no-op (own IS the kernel). Bare lookup is unchanged —
defaulting it to kernel would break a consumer reading its OWN specs, so the flag is the reader's explicit
escape on a collision, not a handbook-wide rewrite.

**Also auto-read `MEMORY.md`** (repo root — the project-local, non-authoritative buffer; SPEC-0039,
split out of SPEC-0007 §6): the Controller / interactive / auto session reads it at startup under
**SPEC-0039**; a dispatched WORKER (`session start --type build`) does **NOT** auto-read it
(SPEC-0039 §0). SPEC-0039 is the authority (`bin/yitc-v2 graph query SPEC-0039`; the file's own
header is a summary of it) for what the reader does with it: TWO entry kinds — an unmarked **short
to-do-NOW line** and an explicitly-marked **bounded temporary instruction** (`[instruction]
[audience: …] [until: …]`); the **READ-ONLY self-filter** at startup — ignore entries whose audience
is not you or whose lifetime has passed, and an UNMARKED note is a plain to-do-NOW line, NOT an
instruction (it cannot grant a standing-action mandate); and consume-once deletion — the session
that CONSUMES an entry DELETES it as a governed WRITE at that moment, never a startup write, never
deferred.

**MANDATORY — scan `bin/yitc-v2 --help`** (`task` / `audit` / `graph --help` for subcommands) — the CLI is the only exhaustive, current list of available verbs; the handbook prose names them by use, but the surface grows per shipped task. This scan is **required, not advisory, before your first guarded work verb**: `--help` emits a session fetch-receipt and `worktree new` / `task file` / `land` (whichever fires first) REFUSE until this session has scanned it (`_require_help_read`) — the enforcement backstop for the class-#17 adoption gap that a pure-advice line could not close. Run it after `bin/yitc-v2 session start`, **carrying your session ref** — `YITC_SESSION_REF=<the ref `session start` printed> bin/yitc-v2 --help` (a `-C` consumer: `YITC_SESSION_REF=<ref> <engine>/bin/yitc-v2 -C <repo> --help`) — because the fetch-receipt is SESSION-TIED: it is credited ONLY after THIS session's own first `session_started`, so a scan run WITHOUT the carry, or before `session start`, is not credited and the guarded verb refuses. One credited scan serves the session: a repeat `session start` in the same context epoch does not ask for another, and the post-`/compact` rescan is named by the re-fold block (§After `/compact`). Journal `event` appends (incl. deviation capture) and `cross *` appends need no scan. **Startup done-when (SPEC-0007 §5b).** Startup is DONE once (1) your audience's seed is read and (2) `session start` has run — the `startup done …` line it prints last (just before the person-facing line) also names the scan for your first guarded work verb. Then open NOTHING else at startup: every other echo line states its class — `[report-only]` (no action now), `[owner-cued]` (only on the owner's cue — a hand-off, a Controller's own-resume) or `[on-demand: <trigger>]` (only when that trigger happens); the seed lines are the read itself.

**`--help` is the verb INVENTORY; the canonical write-flow lives in `§Writes happen in a worktree`** — the ONE home for the worktree-isolated path every mutating action follows. `session start` surfaces it as one entry of the `binding:[seed]` general-verb seed line (SPEC-0007 §5a seed class / SPEC-0051). The generated line delivers each seed rule's startup cue plus a retrieval pointer; full bodies are read when their surface becomes relevant, before the governed action (Single-SoT — SPEC-0005 rule 8: the cue is derived from the rule, the body stays its home).

**[REF_AVAILABLE]** Need a consolidated report (rules, verb governance, …)? Run **`bin/yitc-v2 graph query --type view`** to discover the saved query-lenses FIRST, instead of re-assembling one bespoke under load ( — discovery rests on a deterministic catalog, not AI memory).

**Deviation capture — HOLD ALL SESSION.** The moment something is not as it should be — a manual fallback because no verb covered the case, a redundant re-read, a duplicate tool call, an artifact contradiction — emit `deviation_captured` **immediately**: `bin/yitc-v2 event deviation_captured --data '{"relates_to":…,"impact":…,"fingerprint":…}'` (`kind` is OPTIONAL at capture — decided in triage — normative home SPEC-0056 §1; established by §2). That payload shape is the whole format: do NOT search prior deviation rows for a format or for duplicates first — triage dedups. **No worktree needed** — run the `event` append from anywhere, INCLUDING the main checkout; the line is folded into main by the next `land` ( — see §Writes-happen-in-a-worktree EXCEPTION). Capture is a **reflex, not a judgement** — do NOT pre-decide "is it worth it" (that judgement is exactly what kept frictions invisible). **Invert it: the felt "not worth capturing" hesitation IS itself the trigger — emit first, let triage decide value later.** And if the owner (or any external prompt) had to surface a deviation you'd already noticed and silently passed on, the reflex already MISSED — capture it now AND mark `captured_via: owner-surfaced` so the miss stays countable (class **E-0044**). ONE event, no RCA in the moment; most stay event-only and never become a case file. Silently working around a deviation makes the recurrence invisible and it costs again. (`friction_captured` is the retired legacy name — read-only.) Full procedure (aspect-audits, promotion, case files): `patterns/error-friction-tracking.md`. **Pre-claim premise-false corollary (SPEC-0133):** a **dispatched worker** that finds — BEFORE `worktree new` — that its ready task's PREMISE is false does not exit on the capture: it runs `bin/yitc-v2 task refuse T-XXXX --reason <why>` (what the verb records and how the fleet then reads it: the head of `bin/yitc-v2 task refuse --help`).

**Verb-execution discipline — MANDATORY, HOLD ALL SESSION.** Where a CLI verb **covers** an action — it is the governed path that produces that action's required journal + artifact side-effects — that verb is the **only obligatory path**; doing its work **by hand is FORBIDDEN**. Hand-work skips the verb's deterministic journal emit, so the governed action is **invisible across sessions** — work the journal never saw did not, for the system, happen (the failure / closed). The verb inventory is `bin/yitc-v2 --help` / the graph, **never enumerated here** (the surface grows; enumerating it here would drift). **Narrow exceptions:** (a) **emergency mode** — the tooling itself is broken (`patterns/emergency-mode.md`); (b) a **genuine gap** — no verb covers the case. This is the operational expression of Principle 2 (no substantive action without durable capture) + Principle 5 (one journal). **Mid-turn owner decision — record it AS it arrives.** An owner decision that lands MID-TURN gets no parser-born owner row, so it cannot later authorize an `audit decide`. The reflex: at once, `bin/yitc-v2 event owner_directive` with `captured_via: controller-delegated`, `mid_turn: true`, and `--source-ref <transcript>#uuid:<entry>` — the verb records that entry's COMPLETE text as `owner_text` (credential shapes are redacted on write — SPEC-0163 §4e); a supplied `owner_text` must equal it. Rule home: SPEC-0204 rule 2.

**V2 self-contained protocol.** This repo-local handbook (CHARTER + the AGENTS protocol
(AGENTS-STARTUP.md + AGENTS-SESSIONS.md + AGENTS-PROTOCOL.md) + LIFECYCLE + QUEUE + GRAPH) is **authoritative** for AI session behaviour when cd-ed into
`<repo-root>/`. Global server surfaces — `<host-home>/<vendor-adapter>.md`,
`<host-home>/MEMORY.md`, `<host-home>/<provider-config>/commands/`, `<host-home>/yitc-workspace/`,
`<host-home>/registry.yaml`, `<host-home>/bin/` — are **non-normative read-only provenance**
unless explicitly cited by a V2 artifact (decision YAML / task YAML / spec / handbook section).
V2 entry skill lives single-SoT at `<v2>/<provider-config>/commands/yitc.md`; global
`~/<provider-config>/commands/yitc.md` = thin 2-step pointer (cd + Read project-local).
See full isolation contract + cross-territory cleanup list.

**Session log awareness.** The primary AI tool writes a durable, per-session transcript artifact to a provider-specific local path (typically `~/<tool-config-dir>/.../<session-uuid>.{jsonl,json}` — exact location varies by tool). It records every owner message, AI response, and tool call with timestamps, append-only, persisting across `/compact`. This artifact = **transient input for parser/adapter**, NOT durable citation target. For chat-derived rationales (Principle 2) cite materialized journal entries (`events.jsonl#source_ref=<locator>` or `events.jsonl#ts=<ISO>`). Materialization happens via parser/adapter sync.

**Bare session-log pointer permitted ONLY for routine low-stakes forensic reference**, NOT load-bearing governance.
For load-bearing citations cite the materialized journal entry (verbatim excerpts captured there as a side-effect of materialization).
A bare pointer older than the transcript retention window may dangle once the raw file is pruned — cite the digest or a materialized journal entry instead (`lessons/provider-transcript-archive.md`).
Recovery verb: `bin/yitc-v2 journal sync --session-ref <id>` for orphan-tail forensic cases.

### Journal — know it + query on demand (recovery is one use)

The journal (`events.jsonl`) is a first-class capability, **peer to the graph** — a queryable
record of **intent + action + reads** across sessions. Reach for it ON DEMAND (not per action) for:

- **Orientation** — what was recently directed / done / discussed (incl. by parallel sessions).
- **Prior-art / anti-reinvention (#5)** — «did we already discuss or decide this?» — catches
  discussions that never became an artifact.
- **Cross-session coordination** — the shared truth of concurrent work; no single transcript has it.
- **Intent-vs-actual** — `owner_directive` (intent) vs `commit_landed` / `task_closed` (action);.
- **Recovery** — finding a lost artifact/discussion (the search order below).

Query via **`bin/yitc-v2 journal query`** (parity with `graph query`) — `--type` / `--task` /
`--session` / `--grep` / `--since` / `--limit`. It is the **segment-aware** reader: the journal is ONE
logical history across bounded physical segments (SPEC-0190 rule 1), so a raw text search of the journal PATH
sees the live segment alone and reports an older row as absent.

**Recovery search order** — «Not in `tasks/`/`decisions/`/`plans/`» ≠ «doesn't exist». Before
concluding absence, sweep in THIS order (most decisive first):

1. **Owner-directive journal FIRST** — `bin/yitc-v2 journal query --type owner_directive` (the
   `.yitc/` hook-tail's `owner_input`, which is out of the segment contract — SPEC-0190 rule 1b — and
   is still grepped directly). It records the request's **original wording verbatim** (credential shapes redacted — SPEC-0163 §4e), so query it in
   the **language the owner used** (`--grep <phrase>`) — an artifact may be authored in a different
   language than the ask.
2. **The journal** by `--type` / `--task`; **`git log --all -S<term> --grep`** (commits + `from:` trailers).
3. **Artifact bodies** (`plans/` `decisions/` `ideas/`) — search by BOTH the question's words
   **and** likely solution words. Filenames encode the **solution** framing, not the question, so
   title-match misses.
4. **Provider transcripts** + `.yitc/discussion-drafts-pending/raw-*.md` — LAST. Cross-session work
   lives in the shared **journal**, not in any single session's transcript.

The awareness-ledger (`.yitc/awareness-ledger-current-session.yaml`) holds **read-receipts only** —
which atoms were loaded — NOT discussion content; useless for «what did we discuss».

**Verification:** before your first SUBSTANTIVE action — any edit/write, or any mutating/governed command (the read-only startup calls a session's own `session start` needs are exempt) — voice BOTH anchors aloud in your response — (1) the **anti-complexity** principle (CHARTER §Principle 1), (2) the **deviation-capture reflex** (capture the moment something is not as it should be — / above; full procedure `patterns/error-friction-tracking.md`). One principle is not enough — both must be held from the start. If you cannot voice both, re-read.

## After `/compact`

**Step 1 — the restoration brief.** Unless a `RESTORATION BRIEF` is already in your context (the in-repository post-compaction entry prints it), FIRST run `bin/yitc-v2 session start --print-only`: it prints who you are, what you hold, what was pending and the steps that apply to THIS session, each with its command — act on each. It stamps nothing, so governed verbs stay refused until step 3.

**Step 2 — re-read your audience's whole seed** EXACTLY as at **§At session start** — from the SOURCE manifest **<!--GEN:read-order:arrow generated from HANDBOOK_READ_ORDER — DO NOT EDIT; regen via `graph build`-->CHARTER.md → AGENTS-STARTUP.md → AGENTS-SESSIONS.md → AGENTS-PROTOCOL.md → LIFECYCLE.md → QUEUE.md → GRAPH.md<!--/GEN:read-order-->** (the floor trigger-map `graph/floor-trigger-map.md`), never a subset: a `/compact` is a context-eviction event that may evict ANY mandatory-tier file (SPEC-0007 §5). Restore seed CONTENT by *re-reading*, never by a `session start` run. **Per-audience re-delivery (SPEC-0007 §5c + SPEC-0127).** A dispatched Worker (`--type build`) re-reads its whole `core`+`worker` seed — **`graph/worker-seed.md` AND every continuation part it chains to** (re-reading part 1 alone is the sub-subset the §5b invariant forbids); the interactive Controller re-reads the SOURCE parts directly, in the read-order.

**Co-design MUST (pointer — SPEC-0007 §5b).** This re-read list is the post-`/compact` home for ALL startup-delivered content, not just the handbook files. So any change that adds/changes what `session start` delivers (a file, the `binding:[seed]` seed how-to, the type-dispatch, an echo line) must co-design its post-`/compact` re-delivery in the SAME change — per the §5b coherence invariant. Full rule body lives single-SoT in SPEC-0007 §5b (`bin/yitc-v2 graph query SPEC-0007`); not restated here.

**Refresh the seed_read receipt (per SPEC-0007 §5b / SPEC-0050 §8) — step 3, the stamping run.** A `/compact` advances the context epoch, so every governed/mutating verb refuses `seed_read_stale_epoch` until you refresh the receipt. AFTER the seed re-read above, **re-run `bin/yitc-v2 session start` ONCE per checkout** your next governed verbs run from (a dispatched Worker: **`bin/yitc-v2 session start --type build`** — a bare re-run records the session as a controller), with the same session ref. The receipt is credited from that checkout and the main checkout only, so a Worker that refreshed in its task worktree runs the same command once more in the main checkout before `land`.

**Seed cues come back with the receipt refresh (SPEC-0007 §5b).** That run re-prints the generated `binding:[seed]` line, so each seed rule's cue returns from the same carrier as at start. The STATE re-folds below stay separate and required.

**Stage-bundle freshness (per SPEC-0007 §5a).** A session with an active task + `current_stage` (a Worker, or the Controller self-executing on owner say-so) re-delivers that stage's bundle — `bin/yitc-v2 stage <current_stage> --task T-XXXX`, which a `session start` in the task worktree also delivers; a session with no active lifecycle stage does a seed-only re-read. This reuses the existing post-compact re-read discipline; it is NOT a new gate.

**That re-run prints the post-compact re-fold steps (SPEC-0007 §5b).** On a start whose context epoch is newer than this session's previous start, `session start` prints one re-fold block listing only the steps that apply to this session's state (the brief's last section prints the same steps) — act on each line it prints. The STATE re-folds it can name beyond the steps above, each body in its own spec (pointers only, P5):
- the `--help` rescan, carrying your session ref;
- **Shared coordination-log re-fold (per SPEC-0086):** `bin/yitc-v2 cross outbox` / `cross inbox`;
- **Proactive-debt echo re-fold:** `bin/yitc-v2 debt` (SPEC-0119);
- **External-auditor hint re-fold:** `bin/yitc-v2 audit status` (SPEC-0202);
- `-C` consumer: the frontend-error echo re-fold `bin/yitc-v2 -C <repo> frontend-errors`, invoked bare (SPEC-0171); the kernel-signaling reflex `bin/yitc-v2 graph query --kernel SPEC-0085`; a kernel contract by `graph query --kernel SPEC-XXXX`;
- **MCP reconcile re-delivery:** not a startup step — before the session's first MCP connect/use, compare the connected MCP servers with the project's committed MCP config and report any extra to the person (`bin/yitc-v2 graph query SPEC-0118`);
- **Capture-routing:** at the moment of a capture, the view `bin/yitc-v2 graph query capture-routing` (SPEC-0157).

**Verification:** after compact, before your first SUBSTANTIVE action — any edit/write, or any mutating/governed command (the read-only startup calls a session's own `session start` needs are exempt) — confirm you've re-read your audience's seed VIEW (which carries CHARTER §Principle 1) by voicing BOTH anchors aloud in your response — (1) the **anti-complexity** principle (CHARTER §Principle 1), (2) the **deviation-capture reflex** (full procedure `patterns/error-friction-tracking.md`). One principle is not enough. If you cannot voice both, re-read.

## Language

- **Owner-facing communication** (chat replies, briefs, owner-directed messages / pings) — **Russian**.
- **Code, commits, and identifiers** (source, commit messages, task / decision / spec IDs, event & verb names, YAML field keys) — **English**.

This is V2's OWN rule, no longer inherited from the non-normative global `<host-home>/<vendor-adapter>.md` : AGENTS-STARTUP.md is part of the always-loaded session seed, so a `/clear`'d V2 session that holds **zero** global context still has it. **Distinct concern** from CHARTER §Principle 4b (provider-neutral *methodology text* — no provider brand names in normative docs); see it there, this section does not restate it.

---

> **This protocol continues in two more SOURCE parts** (the AGENTS protocol is split for single-Read safety per SPEC-0120): **AGENTS-SESSIONS.md** (Session types) then **AGENTS-PROTOCOL.md** (Worker protocol through Recommendation Default). Both are listed in `HANDBOOK_READ_ORDER`: a Worker receives them inside its assembled view (the `graph/worker-seed.md` part chain); the Controller reads them directly as the next SOURCE parts of its read-order (SPEC-0007 §5c).
